findings.source_quote: ὡς καὶ Βρεττανοὶ ἐμφανῶς ἐπὶ πάντων κοινωνοῦσι καὶ οὐκ αἰδοῦνται
findings.english_quote: So too Britons openly share with one another in front of everyone and feel no shame.
findings.issue: The generic English “share with one another” obscures the contextual sexual sense of κοινωνοῦσι. This example follows intercourse with mothers and concerns conduct practiced publicly without shame. The absence of an explicit object warrants leaving wives or partners unspecified, but does not require reducing the verb to ordinary sharing. The note discusses possible objects without adequately distinguishing sexual intercourse from communal sexual sharing.
findings.suggested_revision: A contextual candidate is: “So too Britons openly have intercourse in front of everyone and feel no shame.” Explain in a source-quoted note that κοινωνοῦσι literally expresses sharing or participation and may emphasize communal sexual sharing; no particular wives or partners are named. Review the revised wording independently.

findings.source_quote: Οὕτως σοι δοκεῖ τὰ κατὰ τὸν πονηρὸν εἶναι, εἰπέ μοι.
findings.english_quote: Is this how matters concerning the evil one seem to you? Tell me.
findings.issue: The draft selects an interrogative reading without disclosing the alternative declarative reading. The supplied edition joins the opening clause to “tell me” with a comma and ends with a full stop. Greek can support an unmarked question here, particularly beside the imperative, so the draft is not automatically indefensible; nevertheless, the difference between asking Peter to confirm his position and stating his position before requesting further explanation is material. The existing notes do not address that choice.
findings.suggested_revision: Either use the print-aligned candidate, “This is how matters concerning the evil one seem to you; tell me,” or retain the question with a source-quoted note preserving the declarative alternative and explaining the contextual reason for the interrogative reading. Treat the supplied punctuation as an editorial feature, not an OCR error. Any revised text or disclosure requires fresh review.
